correctness.rationale: Expansion gives D=d-aε0+ε1 and W=(cs-ε0)^2, with an a.s. nonzero denominator. Below cutoff D is uniformly positive. At cutoff only one square corner has D=0, where W→b²>0; a two-dimensional triangle scaling gives the exact t^-2 constant. Above cutoff the zero line cuts a positive-length square segment, and conditional interval widths give the exact t^-1 constant. Tail integration yields the sharp absolute-moment cutoffs. A change of corner coordinates, uniformly integrable numerator remainder and an exact double integral prove the log risk divergence. The extracted standard-library verifier independently checks 32,008 exact and numerical assertions; finite checks are not substitutes for proof.

value.rationale: Inexact fixed-point evaluations are a central stability concern. This exact, natural scalar model shows that bounded noise does not by itself make unregularized acceleration moment-safe: there is a quantitative support-amplitude boundary at which the tail exponent changes and mean-square risk diverges logarithmically. The critical cutoff and constants offer a reproducible stress test for denominator safeguarding, rather than a routine local Taylor estimate or arbitrary parameter slice.
